claim: The untrained SFT policy completes the full task under its own sampling noise, and does so more often than ANY reinforcement-learned checkpoint. Under the deterministic mean action it is nearly inert.

successful_conditions.note: all four are coherent full sequences reach->grasp->lift->plate->success

within_demo_ranges.verdict: the four successes sit inside the demonstration distribution; the RL carries do not

identical_weights_check: Both step-0 evaluations run the untouched SFT policy before any gradient update; train_sac.py calls evaluate('init', 0) and evaluate('init_stochastic', 0, deterministic=False) back to back. The ONLY difference is deterministic mean action vs sampling at std 0.20.
consequences: The deterministic evaluation protocol used for the whole SAC-vs-RLPD comparison systematically understates the SFT baseline, which is the reference the RL arms are supposed to improve on.
No RL checkpoint at any budget in any seed ever reaches the plate stage or a full success. The only full successes in the entire experiment come from the UNTRAINED policy.
'RL raises grasp from 0.02 to 1.00' is true but incomplete: RL raises the early stage while eliminating the downstream sequence.
open_question: Whether sampling helps because exploration noise breaks a deterministic deadlock (e.g. a stuck contact), or because the SFT mean action is a poor summary of a multimodal action distribution. Not resolvable from metrics; needs the rendered rollouts.

replication_2026_08_20.what: 25 freshly rendered stochastic rollouts of the untouched SFT policy on the frozen 25-condition prefix. Independent RNG stream, corrected horizontal metric (v1.1), every rollout verified against its raw trajectory.
replication_2026_08_20.agreement_with_trainer: trainer step-0 sweep gave success 0.16 / carry 0.28; this independent draw gives 0.16 / 0.24. The RATE replicates.
replication_2026_08_20.third_confirmation_that_noise_drives_suc: Three independent draws succeeded on three disjoint condition sets -- {11,14,16,18}, {5,9,20}, {0,4,6,9} -- while the rate held near 0.12-0.16. Success is caused by the sampled action noise, not by the initial condition.

transport_quality_true_geometry.note: horizontal displacement computed from true final piston pose, not a bound
transport_quality_true_geometry.verdict: horizontal transport sits inside the demonstration range in all four; lift is inside for cond0/4 and slightly above for cond6/9; ratio inside for three of four.

visual_inspection.observed: piston upright in socket at frame 0 (stage -, disp 0.008 m); grasped and lifted by frame 120 (stage lift, disp 0.249 m, lift 0.212 m, socket visibly empty); stage success from frame 207 with the socket vacated and the piston transported.
visual_inspection.caveat: The piston is small in frame and the TERMINAL placement over the hole plate is not crisply resolvable at this camera angle. Grasp, lift and horizontal transport are directly visible; the final placement is corroborated by the simulator success predicate and the recorded geometry rather than read off the video.
